name: Data.inner_iotaAtLevel
summary: Inner products of algebraic forms are the index of the level times #WeylIndex times Petersson products; the forms associated with iotaAtLevel are the chain of lifts.

steps.claim: Not a step of the proof: lines 42–44 are the rest of the statement, which ends before the `:=` on line 44 (a second-reader message). The line census takes the `:=` of `let u :=` on line 42 for the start of the value, so the check requires these lines to be owned here. They state: with u = weightedChain(triangleOrder(D, false), triLift(D, false), ϑ, 0, m): ⟨iotaAtLevel(D, ϑ)(x), iotaAtLevel(D, ϑ)(y)⟩ = stdLevelIndex(levelOf(lastResLevel(D, ϑ)))·#WeylIndex(Y(D, m), columnsY(D))·⟨u(x), u(y)⟩.
⟨·, ·⟩ of the algebraic forms is the index of the level times #WeylIndex times the Petersson product (`LevelPlaces.LevelForm.inner_eq_petersson` with `Data.isHCParam_Y`).

The level of iotaAtLevel(D, ϑ) is levelOf(lastResLevel(D, ϑ)), and the associated forms are the chain u of lifts (unfolding weightedChain, triangleOrder and triangleModulus, `Space.ofAlgForm_toAlgForm`).
steps.lean:
congr <;> simpa [weightedChain, triangleOrder, triangleModulus,
    LevelPlaces.card_GL_levelModulus] using! (D.spaceY _).ofAlgForm_toAlgForm D.isHCParam_Y _
